tree.SUMMARY: displays sorted directory tree - special graphics for VTxxx terminals.
tree.INSTALLATION: Program      : Just copy the file "tree" into the "/dd/CMDS" directory.

space.PURPOSE: displays effective disk usage of files/dirs
space.SUMMARY: Shows effective disk usage (contents plus file system overhead) of given directory trees and single files. SPACE provides options to find out if some files will fit on a disk with different cluster size than the source.
space.REFERENCES: SPACE functionally replaces the "du" (disk usage) utility
space.INSTALLATION: Program      : Just copy the file "space" into the "/dd/CMDS" directory. On-line-Help : Copy the files "space.hlp" and "space.ndx" into the "/dd/SYS/HELP" directory, if you have my HELP-utility (see EFFO Forum 10) installed. If not, you can read the "space.hlp" file using "list" or any text editor.

space.HISTORY: V1.0         : first working version V1.1, Ed#5   : current version

help.COMMENT: *********************************************************************** *     This file is a so-called "Info" file describing a piece of      * *   software in a standarized way using EFFO's "Info" file format.    * *     The format provides all basic information about a program       * *   in a well structured manner allowing automatic extraction         * *   of important short-form data for databases and software lists     * *   but including more detailed descriptions as well.                 * *     The structure is formed by a set of keywords dividing the       * *   information into different paragraphs (see syntax description     * *   below).                                                           * *                                                                     * *     All programs distributed by EFFO will include such a file.      * *   It will be called Info_xxxx, where xxxx is the program's name.    * *   EFFO encourages all its members and all forum participants as     * *   well as commercial suppliers of OS-9 and OS-9000 software to      * *   use this format to describe their software.                       * *     An empty "form" for Info files called "Info_empty_form" will    * *   be distributed with all EFFO disk and through the OS9-BBS.        * *                                                                     * *     The syntax is quite simple: Each paragraph begins with a        * *   "keyword line" which is a line with a $-Sign in the very first    * *   column immediately followed by the keyword itself. The rest of    * *   the line is reserved for short comments about the paragraph's     * *   purpose. Some paragaphs are mandatory, and some are restricted    * *   in size to ensure that reliable database entries can be           * *   extracted from the file.                                          * *     All subseqent lines up to the next keyword line (or the         * *   end-of-file) are forming the paragraph body, i.e the information  * *   that belongs to the keyword.                                      * *     The order in which the keywords appear in the text (if they     * *   appear at all for optional paragraphs) is free with one           * *   important exception: "$PROGRAM-NAME" must always be the first     * *   keyword in the program description. This rule allows multiple     * *   descriptions to be merged into a single text file without using   * *   special delimiters in between.                                    * *     Finally, "$COMMENT" paragraphs are provided to include          * *   any information not related to a program description, like        * *   this text. They can appear anywhere in the file, even before      * *   the first "$PROGRAM-NAME".                                        * ***********************************************************************
help.SUMMARY: The advanced HELP utility offers structured access to all type of help texts in OS-9/68k systems. The program replaces the standard utility called "help".
help.OS-VERSION: OS-9/68k V1.2 or higher, OS-9000 planned
help.DOCUMENTATION: Help file and Read_Me in english.
help.RUNTIME-FILES: CMDS/help         The help utility CMDS/helpindex    Index file creator utility SYS/HELP/help.hlp The help file for help itself (=documentation) SYS/HELP/*.hlp    Additional help files SYS/HELP/*.hlib   Additional help libraries
help.DOCUMENTATION-FILES: Read_Me           general information Info              This File SYS/HELP/help.hlp A help file describing help itself
help.SOURCE-FILES: help.c            Source for the help utility helpindex.c       Source for the helpindex utility
help.COMPILATION: cc help.c   or  cc helpindex.c , resp.
help.AUTHOR-INFO: Hofenstrasse 12 CH-8708 Maennedorf eMail:  zeller@ethz.uucp zeller@strati.ethz.ch ...cernvax!ethz!zeller DECNet: 57390::ZELLER (PSI%4991108411::STRATI::ZELLER)
help.CONDITIONS: 1. This Program may only be used for peaceful applications. I do NOT ALLOW using this program for anything that has to do with development, testing or manufacturing of weapons of any type. 2. This text as well as all copyright messages (in this file as well as in the source texts and the code files) must be retained. 3. When distributing this program, source code may or may not be included, but the file "help.hlp" as well as the index creator utility "helpindex" HAVE TO be included. 4. Modified or enhanced versions of the program may only be distributed if they are compatible with the original help file format described in this file. Extensions to the help file format must be clearly documented in this file.
help.COPYRIGHT: HELP and HELPINDEX (c) 1989 by Lukas Zeller, CH-Maennedorf
help.INSTALLATION: Copy the help utility "help" into the CMDS directory and all "*.hlp" and "*.hlib" files into the SYS/HELP directory. Then type "help help" and read the documentation about help itself carefully.
help.DESCRIPTION: Refer to the "help.hlp" file (type "help help" when help is installed)

disktest.SUMMARY: This program measures the read and write transfer rates for the current diskdrive (chd). In a second part the maximum and average seek times are caluculated.
disktest.OS-VERSION: developed using V2.3, should run all OS-9/68k versions
disktest.RUNTIME-FILES: creates a large temorary file which is delete at program termination
disktest.COMPILATION: cc -qO=2 disktest.c -l=/dd/lib/os9lib.l   (C V3.2) cc -q disktest.c -l=/dd/lib/os9lib.l      (older versions)
disktest.RESTRICTIONS: will not work on small RAMdisks of fast systems

hist.SUMMARY: This program simulates the 'history'-feature of the BSD-UNIX C-shell. Furthermore a commandline editor gives a bit more comfort in correcting and modifying than 'erase by backspacing'.
hist.HARDWARE: ready to go for Steinmann & Frei's emulation of Wyse-50 terminal on mc68000; may be recompiled for original terminal driver of mc68000 with 2. makefile; may be adapted for any other system and terminal by editing the include files 'h_def.h' and 'h_edidef.h'.
hist.SCREEN-INTERFACE: refer to paragraph 'HARDWARE'; I apologize for not using termcap.
hist.RUNTIME-FILES: uses /r0 for temporary file; may be changed in 'h_def.h'
hist.SOURCE-FILES: h_edit.c h_expand.c h_main.c h_rw.c h_term.c h_def.h h_edidef.h h_var.h
hist.COMPILATION: make                   for Wyse-50 emulation (Steinmann&Frei), mc68000 make -f=make.mcterm    for original terminal driver mc68000 edit sources (esp. *.h), then use makefile
hist.HISTORY: first developed on CP/M-68k in 1987, then ported to OS-9/68k
hist.EXPANSION: no expansion planned by the author
hist.INSTALLATION: may be taken as the initial process while logging in ( -> password )
hist.EXPERIENCES: The author has developed this program using the CP/M-68k OS, ported it to OS-9/68k using the genuine terminal driver of the mc68000. That version was hardware dependant because it used a special memory location to allow insert mode while editing the commandline. All worked fine (as far as I can remember). After getting the Wyse-50 emulation of Steinmann&Frei the program was adapted to this terminal. Hardware dependecy could be removed because insert mode can be switched on and off by Escape sequences. Shortly after this adaption I got the 'ZSH' written by Lukas Zeller, which I use since that time (about 1.5 years ago) instead of my own history/editing aid, because it seems more powerful to me.

compress.SUMMARY: The compress program is compatible with the compression/decompression used on the Unix systems compress programs. This is version 4 and supports up to 16 bits compression.
compress.PROJECT: The porting retained the Unix meanings of all options, added a couple for MsDos and modified the file name conventions to make more sense.
compress.REFERENCES: The algorithm is taken from "A Technique for High Performance Data Compression", Terry A. Welch, IEEE Computer Vol 17, No 6 (June 1984), pp 8-19. Modified Lempel-Ziv method (LZW). Basically finds common substrings and replaces them with a variable size code. This is deterministic, and can be done on the fly. Thus, the decompression procedure needs no input table, but tracks the way the table was built.
compress.SOURCE-FILES: PROG: compress.h, compress.c, compress.fns, compapi.c, compusi.c
compress.SOURCE-PREREQUISITES: LIB: os9lib.l DEFS/SYS: file.h, stat.h, types.h, uio.h
compress.COMPILATION: Use delivered makefile. ATTENTION: Be aware that all required directories are available
compress.HISTORY: Author(s): Initials  Name DjG     Donald J. Gloistein / Plus many others, see rev. history LvR     Lyle V. Rains Revision History: version -- date -- Notes 4.01    08-29-88  DjG  first cut for 16 bit MsDos version 09-04-88  DjG  fixed unlink on zcat if interupted. added msdos filename logic and functions 4.10    10-27-88  DjG  revised API with coding changes by LvR. 4.10a   10-30-88  DjG  cleaned up code and fixed bug in freeing ptr. 4.10b   11-01-88  DjG  cleaned up the logic for inpath/outpath Changed the logic to finding the file name Fixed the allocation bug in the api Added some more portability macros 4.10c   11-04-88  DjG  Changed maxcode from global to static in api. Supplied some library functions for those who don't have them, changed dos usi to use the strrpbrk(). Checked casts in api again. Compiles without warnings at pick level 3. 4.10d   11-25-88  DjG  revised some memory allocation, put more in the header file. Corrected some typos. Changed prog_name() to force lower case Corrected bug, no longer unlinks existing file if not enough memory to compress or decompress 12-06-88  DjG  VERY minor changes for casts and header defines 12-08-88  DjG  Adjusted path separator check in main function Amiga uses split seg because of compiler 12-09-88  DjG  Debugging done, all defaults now Unix compress defaults, including unlinking input file and acting as a filter. Must use -h option to get help screen. 4.10e   12-11-88  DjG  Fixed more casts, prototypes and header file. 4.10f   12-12-88  DjG  Fixed unlinking open files on error. This fails on shared or os/2 platforms. 12-15-88  DjG  Fixed SIGTYPE for function passed to signal Fixed problems with Xenix 2.2.1 4.2     12-19-88  DjG  Replaced adaptive reset as an option. 4.3     12-26-88  DjG  Fixed long file name bug, fixed bug with compressdir. -B option added, same as -b option 05-06-89  Dal  Ported to Sozobon/Alcyon C for Atari ST. Also, created get_one() for console prompting. 05-08-89  Dal  Ported to Minix-ST
compress.INSTALLATION: Copy the program to your execution directory.
compress.EXPERIENCES: Good compression factor (2-3) - depending on source type. Not limited to text sources.
compress.NOTES: The 'tar'-program often will be used together with compress especially on UNIX-tapes. See notes in compress.h for defines needed. It should work now with Xenix. The output is ALLWAYS smaller or equal to the input. For using the delivered makefile the following dir's MUST be sisters: PROG, RELS, DEFS, LIB, CMDS. CAUTION: Because the program is in modules, make sure you recompile all modules if you change the header or a define in the compress.c file. Check the signal() handler functions in your compiler documentation. This code assumes ANSI SYS V compatible header and return values. Change as appropriate for your compiler and operating system. This source compiles properly with Microsoft C compiler version 5.1. Assumptions: When filenames are given, replaces with the compressed version (.Z suffix) only if the file decreases in size.
compress.COMMENT: This code is ported from compress v4.0 release joe.
